clue.text: Odd features of chakra coach

indicators.note: the odd-numbered features of a word are its first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone notices peculiar aspects of a coach trip's yoga energy points.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a railway carriage, which is also called a car, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Professionally transports in theatrical performance; hides in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so what matters is how the words are said

parts.note: a show is a theatrical performance; furs are animal hides

explanation.surface: An actor in a play conceals something during a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' fits the theatre picture but signals a sound-alike. 'in' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur drives people as a job, so chauffeurs is a verb for carrying passengers for pay.

clue.text: Relationship of Vatican with Church of England

parts.note: the Vatican is the seat of the Roman Catholic Church
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: The ties between the Catholic Church and the Anglican Church.
explanation.walkthrough: The ecumenical surface hides a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, a romantic relationship between two people.

clue.text: Pair having argument — one side might lose it after this?

definitions.text: one side might lose it after this?

parts.note: a pair of things that go together is a match
an argument made in debate is a point

explanation.surface: A couple are quarrelling, and one of them may end up losing the row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' just joins the two parts. The definition is cryptic: after the final rally of a tennis match, one player has lost it.
explanation.definitionFit: Match point is the rally that can decide a tennis contest, after which one player or team has been beaten.

clue.text: Row's origin lost in muddle

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its opening letter, which goes missing

parts.note: to row a boat is to paddle

explanation.surface: The cause of a quarrel gets forgotten amid the confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument; it is propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to confuse or befuddle, so as verbs it matches muddle closely.

clue.text: Prostitute can't rouse drunk

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A sex worker is unable to wake a client who has passed out drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a prostitute with wealthy or upper-class clients, especially in historical courts.

clue.text: Guided German guy in selecting Nordic food

indicators.note: these words are placed inside the word for selecting

parts.note: choosing
past tense of lead
Herr is German for Mr

explanation.surface: A tour guide leads a German man as he chooses Scandinavian dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled herring, cured in vinegar, is a staple of Scandinavian and Baltic cuisine, often served at smorgasbords.

clue.text: Teasing out that which was internalised: …

indicators.note: out suggests being sorted out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Teasing out what someone has absorbed inwardly, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 8-down only in the surface reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesta is the technical word for material taken into the body as food, things swallowed and so taken inside.

clue.text: … small amount of information briefly recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run the other way
made brief, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: data is information

explanation.surface: Continuing 7-down, a little information is briefly remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a very little bit, an informal word for a slight quantity.

clue.text: Tight chaperone making needless overtures?

definitions.note: the phrase names the act of making pointless approaches

parts.note: taken as written: the fourteen letters to be rearranged
in a reverse clue, the letters before have been made into something new, which the answer states as its own last word

explanation.surface: A strict chaperone makes pointless advances, or pointless overtures to a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer describes the clue. Rearrange the letters of 'Tight chaperone' and you get the first three words, which have been converted.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes arguing a case to listeners who already share your view, so the persuasive approach is wasted effort.

clue.text: Esteemed flier stuck on the ground

parts.note: a flier is a printed advertisement, shortened to ad
stuck in mud or bog

explanation.surface: A respected pilot or bird finds itself grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests an aircraft or bird, but here it is a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be esteemed is to be held in high regard, which is what being admired means.

clue.text: Friendly uncle grew up free as a bird?

parts.note: unc is a familiar, chummy shortening of uncle
grew older

explanation.surface: A genial relative matured into a carefree adult.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird let out of its cage is uncaged, so it is literally released and at liberty.

clue.text: Kitty, a psychic zealot

parts.note: a kitty is a pooled sum of money
taken as written
a stage performer who appears to read minds

explanation.surface: A cat named Kitty turns out to be a fanatical clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a pet or a name; it is a shared pot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatic, and a fundamentalist is a strict, uncompromising adherent of a doctrine.

clue.text: Open seat, varied nominees

parts.note: candid means frank

indicators.note: something varied has been changed, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An open seat in an election attracts a diverse field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open seat' looks like a political phrase; 'Open' is frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates are people put forward for election or selection, which is what nominees are.

clue.text: Great footballer retiring, hasn't played for Ivory Coast national team?

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Pelé, the Brazilian football great

indicators.note: letters that are played around with are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A star player retires without ever having turned out for the Ivorian side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ivory Coast football team is nicknamed the Elephants; ivory comes from elephant tusks, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Éléphants is the official nickname of the Côte d'Ivoire football side, and tusk ivory also links the beasts to the country.

clue.text: Lacking energy, cannot rule out sleeping through the day

indicators.note: ruled out of order, so the letters are rearranged
E stands for energy, and lacking it means that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone too tired can't rule out dozing all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal animals are active at night and rest in daylight hours.

clue.text: Shot adult type of film

parts.note: a shot of whisky is a dram
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: Someone describes having shot an adult movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like filming; it is a measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a serious, story-driven genre of motion picture, as opposed to comedy or action.

clue.text: Horse hurdling width of tree

indicators.note: a horse hurdling a fence straddles it, so its letters go either side

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat
W is the abbreviation for width

explanation.surface: A horse jumps across the breadth of a fallen tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree known for its red berries.

clue.text: With more trees and weird enchanted rings within

indicators.note: these go inside the other letters
something under a spell is transformed, so these letters are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written
two rings look like the letter O

explanation.surface: A forest with more trees and strange magic fairy rings inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodier is the comparative of woody, describing land more thickly covered by forest.

clue.text: See 9
Crack across old filling is calamity

indicators.note: these letters stretch across and enclose the filling

parts.note: to have a crack at something is to try it
aged means old; filling says it goes inside

explanation.surface: A tooth with a crack through an ancient filling is a dental disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' and 'filling' paint dentistry; crack is an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a terrible event causing great suffering, a disaster or catastrophe.

clue.text: No rule getting hitchhiker to disembark in border area

parts.note: taken as written
R is a dictionary abbreviation for rule
a hitchhiker thumbs a lift
to come ashore from a ship

explanation.surface: With no rules in force, a hitchhiker is told to get off at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is the English county bordering Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Northumberland is the northernmost county of England, lying along the frontier with Scotland, so it is a border region.

clue.text: This meat's not off, as top cook announced

indicators.note: in a down clue the word placed at the top comes first
something announced is spoken out, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
something not off is on

explanation.surface: A head chef declares this meat has not gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: BAKE placed on top of ON, said out loud, gives the cured meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured meat from the back or sides of a pig, so it is a type of pork.

clue.text: Geoffrey's first tune in Shine

indicators.note: the first of the name means only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: initial letter of the name
to tune in is to listen to a broadcast

explanation.surface: Someone named Geoffrey begins by tuning in to a programme called Shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tune in' looks like part of the surface's radio scene; it is a phrasal verb for paying attention by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle or gleam with reflected light, a close synonym of shine as a verb.

clue.text: Perhaps a Rover's Return idol?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Rover is a classic name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: The Rovers Return is the pub in the British soap Coronation Street, so this sounds like a pub's idol.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or figure worshipped as a deity, so a god.

clue.text: Fraud opening religious community

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a vent is an aperture

explanation.surface: A swindle starts up a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' reads as launching the fraud; it is a noun for a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a house where nuns live together under religious vows, so it is a community of the faithful.

clue.text: Honey sandwich for half-cut valet's tea

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two slices

parts.note: both are terms of endearment

indicators.note: cut in half means only half of the name survives

parts.note: Jeeves is the valet in P. G. Wodehouse's stories

explanation.surface: A sweet snack is made for a valet who is tipsy and wants his tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' means drunk in British slang, but here it removes half of Jeeves, leaving JEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Darjeeling is a fine black tea grown in the Indian hill district of the same name.

clue.text: Pigments losing original character naturally?

indicators.note: the original character is the opening letter, which is dropped

parts.note: dyes are colouring substances

explanation.surface: Colourings lose their original hue, perhaps through natural fading.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'naturally!' in reply is an emphatic agreement, an exclamation equivalent to answering in the affirmative.
